label: verify-bm-4d-printing-review

claims.claim: A vat-photopolymer (SLA/DLP) humidity-actuated 4D part has been published (Small 2024, PEG-polyurethane ink, film folds in under 1 s, 50 um film over 5x faster than 150 um, lifts 50 mg); not a Formlabs resin and no Timoshenko analysis.
claims.source_says: Like a cantilever beam, the film rapidly initiated folding in less than 1s. A film having 50 μm thickness folded over 5 times faster compared to a film of around 150 μm thickness
claims.note: Full text (PMC10922657) confirms the 1 s fold, the 5x thickness effect, the 50 mg/5x load at RH~90%, SLA 400 nm and DLP 380 nm printing, and zero 'Timoshenko' hits; 'not Formlabs' and 'contradicts the earlier gap' are the agent's framing.

claims.claim: The 'stock Formlabs resins gain under 1 percent in 24 h' statement is method-dependent: Flexible 80A V2 gains +8% mass and +3% volume in 1 day in water (ASTM D471 slab); Elastic 50A V2 39.2% IPA vs Rigid 10K under 0.1% is confirmed.
claims.source_says: Flexible 80A V2 TDS, Deionized Water, 1 day: -26 hardness, +8% mass, +3% volume (1 week: -27, +9%, +7%). Solvent page: Elastic 50A Resin V2 IPA 39.2, water 0.7 (24 h weight gain); Rigid 10K <0.1.
claims.note: I read the datasheet page as an image and mapped the solvent-page columns (IPA 10th, water 18th); all numbers reproduce.

claims.claim: No hygromorph/bilayer design constrained by a proof-assistant-checked law was found; arXiv 2604.26367 is 'verified' only in a category-theoretic sense, applies the Timoshenko formula to an FFF polyamide bilayer (36.4 vs 35.3 +/- 3.1 deg), and never mentions Lean, Coq or Isabelle.
claims.source_says: Here we present a category theoretic compositional framework for verified nature-derived design. Baseline (hygroscopic / bending) n=3 Predicted 36.4° Measured 35.3 ± 3.1° 3.0%
claims.note: The preprint parts reproduce (0 hits for Lean, Coq, Isabelle, proof assistant; FFF, PA6-GF/PA612-CF, Timoshenko formula present), but 'none found anywhere' is a search-absence claim I did not independently test.

claims.claim: Humidity-driven polymer actuators are slow and weak compared with thermal SMPs/LCEs: hydrogel forces under 1 N, cellulose-filled FFF bilayers 30 min for full transformation, thin wood 24 h, thick timber about 400 h.
claims.source_says: The bilayers reach a full transformation between two RH extremes of 30% and 90% within 30 minutes. [hydrogel review] swelling and contraction forces for most hydrogel actuators are less than 1 N
claims.note: The individual numbers check out against the Cheng, Chau/Amstad, Rueggeberg and Groenquist texts, but the sweeping 'slow and weak vs thermal' comparison is a judgment, and the same agent's Small 2024 film folds in under 1 s.

overall: Three of four key claims reproduce against primary text. The fourth, the slow-and-weak generalisation, is a mix of reproduced numbers and a judgment. The 'none found' proof-assistant gap is an absence claim I did not test.
